methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines a pooled base-editing screen (n=34 sgRNAs), two biologically independent donors, orthogonal validation with synthetic sgRNAs, scRNA-seq, metabolomics, Seahorse, and NSG xenograft models with repeated independent donors (e.g., n=18–19 mice/arm for Nalm6, n=11/arm for Sh-Sy5y). Appropriate controls (mock, UT, RASA2 positive control, CD19-KO neutral controls) and both hematologic and solid tumor models strengthen rigor. The Methods explicitly state no predetermined sample size calculation, no blinding for in vitro work and only partial blinding for in vivo scoring (operator blinded for condition/survival but not analysis), and no data exclusion. Statistical choices are appropriate (paired/unpaired t-tests with normality testing via Shapiro–Wilk, Wilcoxon alternatives, Mantel–Cox for survival, one-sample tests for normalized data), but multiplicity correction across the many pairwise comparisons and flow panels is not systematically described outside the DEG/omics pipelines; effect sizes beyond means±s.d. are inconsistently reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is preclinical mechanistic and translational work in primary human T cells, cell lines, and NSG xenograft mouse models — Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is nonetheless high: the identified E81K and L32P edits are directly actionable within existing CAR T manufacturing workflows, were validated in CAR T cells from heavily pretreated patients with cancer, and target both hematologic (CD19) and solid (B7H3, L1CAM) tumor contexts with surrogate preclinical efficacy endpoints (survival, tumor burden, persistence). Safety screening (no lymphomagenesis, intact organ histology, no cytokine release signature, cBioPortal survey) further strengthens the near-term translational path toward first-in-human studies, placing it well above a mechanistic-curiosity score.

reporting_quality.justification: Preclinical/animal work is the primary design, so ARRIVE applies most directly (with elements of REMARK-style biomarker reporting also relevant). The manuscript reports mouse strain, sex, age, housing, ethics approvals, randomization after tumor-burden matching, partial blinding (survival/scoring operator blinded; analysis not blinded), humane endpoints, group sizes with donor provenance, and justification for exclusion (tumor-free deaths with unknown cause excluded). Omissions include no a priori sample-size calculation, no formal randomization method, and only partial blinding of imaging analysis. Data availability is strong: bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, and metabolomics are deposited in Zenodo with explicit DOIs (refs 74–76), Galaxy/pysam/nf-core pipelines are named with versions, and Supplementary Tables provide sgRNA sequences and antibodies — though analytical code for custom scripts is not clearly linked.

novelty_literature.justification: The core novelty is conceptual and methodological: performing a CAR-adapted (CAR-coexpressed sgRNA) base-editing screen that identifies CAR-design-specific point mutations in PIK3CD, with E81K and L32P exerting opposite PI3K-signaling effects advantageous to BBz vs 28z CARs respectively. Prior base-editing allelic maps in untransduced T cells (Schmidt et al. Nature 2024; Walsh et al. Nat Biotechnol 2025) are explicitly acknowledged as the closest comparators, and the authors appropriately frame their contribution as the first to show that CAR costimulatory context dictates which allelic tunings are beneficial. This is a meaningful advance beyond prior PI3K/AKT modulation (Klebanoff, Zheng, Cannons) and prior CAR enhancement by KO (RASA2, SUV39H1, TET2, NR4A), but does not establish a wholly new mechanism or first-in-class modality.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with a logical arc from screen design → hit validation → mechanism (signaling, scRNA-seq, metabolomics) → in vivo efficacy → safety → opposite hit for the alternate CAR. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and self-contained; figure captions are detailed, with n, test, and donor provenance consistently stated. Acronyms (CAR, ABD, ABE/CBE, APDS, SCM, EM, CM) are generally defined on first use and terminology is precise. Minor issues: dense Methods paragraphs on omics could be subdivided, some reliance on Extended Data for key supporting data points (e.g., exhaustion marker time courses), and the ROADSTAR acronym is overused and never fully necessary; nonetheless, overall presentation is publication-ready.

key_strengths: CAR-coexpressed base-editing screen is methodologically original and reveals CAR-design-dependent allelic tuning (E81K for BBz, L32P for 28z)
Convergent multi-omic mechanistic support: pAKT phosphoflow, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, HILIC/RP metabolomics, NADH, Seahorse OCR/ECAR, mitochondrial mass
In vivo efficacy demonstrated across two tumor types (Nalm6 leukemia, Sh-Sy5y neuroblastoma) and two CAR targets (CD19, B7H3) with adequate mouse numbers and Mantel–Cox survival analyses
Thorough safety package: long-term follow-up, histology, liver enzymes, serum cytokines, cBioPortal survey — directly addresses current regulatory concerns about T-cell lymphomagenesis
Validation extended to CAR T cells from heavily pretreated patients with cancer, strengthening translational relevance
Transparent data deposition: Zenodo DOIs for scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, and metabolomics; named pipeline versions
key_concerns: No a priori sample-size calculation and no formal randomization procedure described for in vivo studies; in vivo imaging analysis not blinded
Multiplicity correction across the many pairwise flow/functional comparisons is not systematically applied outside omics pipelines
Low biological-donor depth for key omics (scRNA-seq from a single donor; metabolomics from n=3 donors) limits inter-donor generalizability of mechanism
Base-editing efficiencies (~30% for L32P with mono/biallelic mixtures) and residual bystander edits are only partially controlled by haplotype analysis
Safety claim relies on NSG mice (immunocompromised) with ≤66 days follow-up — insufficient to exclude long-term oncogenic risk from an APDS-associated activating variant
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous, mechanistically deep, and translationally salient preclinical CAR-T engineering study with a conceptually novel CAR-adapted screen framework, strong in vivo efficacy and safety data across hematologic and solid tumor models, and transparent data sharing — content consistent with tier-1 oncology venues, pending modest clarifications on in vivo blinding/randomization and multiplicity.
